Exploring Calvert County, Maryland’s Tax Lien Sales

If you’re looking for a great way to invest with the potential for solid returns, Calvert County, Maryland’s tax lien sales might be your next big opportunity. Let’s dive into the details of this investment option.

Why Invest in Tax Liens?

Tax lien investing can offer impressive returns. In Calvert County, the interest rate on tax liens is 10% annually. This is considerably higher than many traditional investment options. Plus, the cost of entry is relatively low, making it accessible for many investors.

Understanding Tax Lien Certificates

When you buy a tax lien certificate, you’re essentially paying off someone else’s unpaid property taxes. In return, you get the right to collect the amount you paid plus interest. If the property owner doesn’t pay back the taxes within a set period, you could potentially foreclose on the property and become the owner.

Steps to Participate

  1. Research and Understand Local Laws: It’s crucial to understand the legal framework surrounding tax lien sales in Maryland and Calvert County.
  2. Visit the Local Treasurer’s Website: Check the Treasurer’s Office website for sale schedules and specific auction details.
  3. Check the Auction Site: The auction typically takes place at the Calvert County Commissioners Hearing Room, 175 Main Street, Prince Frederick, MD.
  4. Read Sale Details: Familiarize yourself with the schedule, parcel inquiries, and other essential details.
  5. Contact the County Office: For additional inquiries, you can contact the Treasurer’s Office directly.

Pro Tips

  • Stay Updated: Tax sale schedules can change, so keep an eye on the official county website for updates.
  • Understand Foreclosure Rules: If the property owner does not redeem the lien, you can initiate foreclosure between six months and two years after the sale.
  • Prepare Your Payment: Be ready to pay with cash, check, or cashier’s check immediately after winning the bid.

FAQs

Q: What if the property is redeemed?

A: You’ll be reimbursed for the taxes and costs paid plus 10% annual interest. If foreclosure proceedings have started, you can also be reimbursed for legal expenses.

Q: How do I start foreclosure?

A: Foreclosure can begin no earlier than six months and a day from the sale date but must be done within two years.

Q: What happens if I don’t foreclose?

A: You forfeit the taxes paid at the sale, your certificate becomes void, and the property may go back to the tax sale.

By understanding these details and following the outlined steps, you can take advantage of the investment opportunities available through Calvert County’s tax lien sales​.
